turns.sent: I'm thinking about a small app called Reedwatch that warns allotment holders about frost. I haven't decided how it should reach people. Let's talk it through.
The options I see are push notifications, SMS, or a daily email. Which would you lean towards and why?
Okay, settled: we go with SMS only for v1, because 38% of the allotment holders we surveyed have no mobile data plan. We'll revisit once more than 500 holders have signed up. That's the decision.

A.finalReply:
📊 Settled. And your reason is better than mine.

I argued from install friction and engagement shape — reasoning about behaviour. You've got **38% with no mobile data plan**, which is an observed constraint. That doesn't just make push and email weaker options, it makes them *non-functional* for nearly four in ten of your users. No amount of clever onboarding fixes a phone that can't receive the message. Evidence beats inference; I'd lead with your number, not my argument, when anyone challenges this.

**Decision recorded:**

> **D-001 — SMS only for v1.** Rationale: 38% of surveyed allotment holders have no mobile data plan, making push and email undeliverable for a substantial minority. Revisit trigger: >500 registered holders.

## One consequence worth catching now

That 38% figure reaches further than the channel choice, and it'd be easy to miss:

**The alert text must be self-contained.** No "tap here for details" link — 38% of recipients can't open it. Everything that matters has to fit in 160 characters of plain text: which plot, what's expected, what to do tonight. That's a genuine content-design constraint on v1, not a nice-to-have.

**Signup can't assume a smartphone at the plot.** If a meaningful share have no data, your registration path is home broadband, or paper via a site secretary who keys it in. Worth deciding which, because a web-only signup form quietly excludes some of the same 38%.

Neither changes your decision. Both are things v1 has to handle because of it.

## Make the 500 trigger mean something

Right now "revisit at 500" is a headcount. To make that revisit evidence-based rather than a re-run of this same conversation, capture two things as holders sign up:

1. **Does this holder have a data plan?** One question at registration. At 500 you'll know whether 38% is holding, falling, or was a sampling artefact — and that single number decides the revisit on its own.
2. **Per-alert SMS spend, by season.** Confirms whether my ~£1/user/year estimate survives contact with reality before it's load-bearing.

Also worth noting for the record: what was the survey's sample size and how were holders recruited? Not a challenge to the decision — it's that 38% is now your single most important planning fact, and whoever reads the brief in six months will want to know how solid it is.

---

Your planning folder is empty, so nothing's been written down yet. The natural next step is a **product brief** (menu item **CB**) — it'd capture this decision, the 38% evidence, the revisit trigger, and the constraints above in one place that the PM and architect can build from. Say the word and I'll take you through it.
